rv.q: It’s a gloriously dusty old piece of propaganda that was fitted out by Rattigan to prove that the spirit of the Blitz could not only see off the dastardly Jerry, but also vanquish the shallow cult of celebrity. … You have to feel a bit sorry for Miller and Purefoy, because the leading roles are a little dull.
Trevor Nunn's magnificent revival of Terence Rattigan's 1942 play is an ensemble achievement.
Nunn's cast, and especially Sheridan Smith, convey this time of teetering on tenterhooks with power and resonance.
